record.title: Sheeb passenger departures suspended during Iranian fuel protests, November 2019
record.scope: Passenger departures toward Iran at one crossing; trade exempt
record.movement: Ordinary passengers leaving Iraq for Iran.
record.imposing_authority: Iraq Border Ports Commission at Iran’s request
record.enforcement: Border commission announced suspension and subsequently reported resumed departures.
record.relationship: Companion post to the Shalamcheh episode R2-ME-005, with a separate reopening; not an independent national decision.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no assumption of continuation to the research cutoff.
record.official_rationale: Protective closure associated with protests in Iran; Iran requested the suspension according to the Iraqi commission.
record.context: Fuel-price protests prompted restrictions at two southern crossings.
record.uncertainty: Both decisive endpoints rely on the commission’s account, repeated by separate publishers. No independent daily post log recovered. Round13 freshly opened NINA onset and reopening accounts confirm the same official lineage; additional publishers do not add independent implementation evidence.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated actual reopening for the specified category and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Only ordinary Iraq-to-Iran passenger departures at Sheeb are eligible; freight was exempt.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Contemporary official-account reports establish the passenger suspension.
November 16 specified at onset and retrospectively on reopening.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Security rationale is attributed through the Iraqi account of Iranian protest conditions.
Commission describes the closed period; no interruption reported, but daily records absent.
